title: Conditional Shadow Traffic and Attenuated Rollout Composer
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We need a single, auditable configuration and policy compiler that supports conditional shadowing, attenuated traffic ramps, probabilistic gating, and automatic rollback triggers for model rollouts across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Current canary DSL supports only linear step schedules and static traffic splits; operators ask for: cohort-level attenuation (different ramp speeds per customer segment), shadow amplifications (temporarily amplify shadow traffic for rare-event detection), conditional shadowing predicates (route to shadow only if request matches a predicate), and configurable rollback confidence windows that combine runtime telemetry with eval metrics.
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a policy composer that compiles a human-friendly DSL into runtime rules for the routing layer. Key capabilities: 1) conditional shadow routes based on predicates (headers, route meta, sampling seed); 2) attenuated step schedules per cohort with independent backoff/forward heuristics; 3) probabilistic gates with tunable exploration fraction; 4) auto-rollback policy that aggregates signals over a configurable confidence window and triggers either staged rollback or full cutover; 5) safety fences (max-surge, min-preserve, dead-man timeout) and a transparent audit trail in console.
acceptance_criteria: DSL compiles to router rules and passes unit tests with >95% coverage
Can define cohort-specific schedules (example: enterprise vs free-tier) and the router applies different ramps in the same deployment
Conditional shadow predicates evaluated at edge with <0.5ms median overhead added
Auto-rollback trigger evaluates composite signal (latency P95, token-error-rate, hallucination proxy) and executes rollback within configured SLA
End-to-end e2e canary run showing shadow amplification catching a synthetic regression (replay test) and rollback executing automatically
rollout_plan: 1) Prototype DSL + compiler (branch in repo) and unit tests; 2) Runtime router adapters: implement shadow predicate evaluator and attenuated-scheduler; 3) Internal canary run on staging with synthetic regressions; 4) Beta with two partner teams (Search and Compose) using small cohorts; 5) Full rollout and Console UI for visualizing policies and recent decisions.
proposed_config_schema_changes: Add top-level 'policies' object with fields: 'id', 'target_cohorts' (list), 'steps' (time/value pairs with attenuation factors), 'shadow' (predicate, amplify_factor, sample_rate), 'gates' (probabilistic fraction, exploration_window), 'rollback' (conditions, confidence_window_seconds, action), and 'safety_fences' (max_surge_percent, min_preserve_percent, deadman_timeout). Compiler will expand into per-router rule file and a human-readable audit summary.
implementation_notes: Router: add lightweight predicate evaluator (JS-like expressions) executed in sandboxed wasm to avoid runtime instability
Compiler: write in Go to reuse existing rollout config codebase, emit v2 rule format expected by router
Telemetry: aggregate composite signals in telemetry service and expose an API for policy evaluation
Console: add policy visualizer with simulated step preview and expected traffic curve
Testing: synthetic regression harness that can inject deterministic errors for shadow amplification validation
